page.layout: One printed page. At the top, a full-width paragraph. Below it, two parallel columns: left, Ianuarius (with Martius beneath it); right, Februarius (with Aprilis beneath it). Each column has a number column on its left and a "Aureus num." column on its right. No margin notes.

main_text.l: Romæ in vetustissimo marmore incisum, teste Luca Gaurico, habes in quatuor prioribus mensibus: octo tamen reliquis mensibus etiam numerum aureum adscribere potes, si lunationi uni, ut fieri solet, alternatim tribuas 30 &c 29[?] dies.

page.notes: The old 5 before "Idus" (left column, 5 Idus) is a bent glyph, read as 5. The figure after "&c" in the top paragraph is hard to read; read as 29 with [?]. The column heads "Ianuarius" and "Februarius" carry "Aureus num." on the right; this is a column heading, not a list line. The leader dashes are not printed text and are not transcribed. The number "186" at top left is printed in old-style figures.
